newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan 1997 govt spending 1.86 bln dinars-minister.
newsitem.headline: Jordan 1997 govt spending 1.86 bln dinars-minister.

text.p: Jordan's Finance Minister Marwan Awad said on Wednesday that projected 1997 state expenditure was 1.860 billion dinars ($2.62 billion), up from a readjusted 1996 budget spending estimate of 1.764 billion dinars.
"The size of the budget (expenditure) of 1997 is 1.860 billion dinars," Awad told Reuters.
He declined to say how big the budget deficit would be next year, but said it would be within targets set by the International Monetary Fund.
The IMF has said the budget should be cut in 1997 to 3.1 percent of GDP from an estimated 4.1 percent in the 1996 budget.
Officials have said the new draft 1997 budget has yet to be finalised by the cabinet before it is submitted to parliament for approval by year-end.
They said a tight rein on public spending will be maintained by a freeze on hiring for public sector jobs.

The tight 1997 budget constraints put in place are critical to the last two years of an accelerated IMF reform programme, ending in late 1998, to further liberalise Jordan's economy and integrate it with global markets.
Officials say the 1996 deficit is not expected to exceed 200 million dinars. This does not factor in foreign assistance which has traditionally covered budget deficit shortfalls.
